Books and Papers, in Reading Order

For Child-Rearing

The Continuum Concept by Jean Liedloff (1975) is a foundational natural-child-rearing book, based on her time with the Ye’kuana. Is it settled anthropology? No, it's provocative observation, so take it with a grain of salt.

Hunt, Gather, Parent by Michaeleen Doucleff (2021) is a practical, accessible book about kids taking part in family life, autonomy, and spreading out the work of caring for them.

Practical Community-Building Guides

Where do you start with the nuts and bolts? Creating a Life Together by Diana Leafe Christian, for membership, money, land and agreements.

Want a guide to intentional community that covers the whole system? There's Building Belonging by Yana Ludwig.

Governance Manuals

Many Voices One Song by Rau and Koch-Gonzalez is a practical manual for doing sociocracy.

Building United Judgment by Schaub and colleagues is about consensus decision-making.

Ludwig and Gimnig's The Cooperative Culture Handbook has a bunch of exercises for being more cooperative, dealing with conflict and building group culture.

What Helps Communities Last—and Whether Longevity Is Enough

Communities That Abide by Dmitry Orlov makes an uncomfortable argument: the communities that last a long time often rely on 1) communal property, 2) separation, 3) boundaries and 4) a binding ideology. From a distance, cohesion and capture can look a lot alike.

Is longevity alone a meaningful measure, when a community may keep going without its members flourishing? That's the question in “Measuring Success in Intentional Communities”, a paper by Rubin, Willis and Ludwig.

Commitment and Community by Rosabeth Moss Kanter is a classic. It compares a bunch of nineteenth-century communes, and the practices that built commitment in them.

Alienation and Charisma by Benjamin Zablocki is field research on communes, and on the role charisma plays in them.

Jo Freeman's “The Tyranny of Structurelessness” (1970) is the classic essay on hidden hierarchy. Can it be harder to challenge than explicit authority? She argues it can.

For the Zapatistas

The Fire and the Word by Gloria Muñoz Ramírez and Subcomandante Marcos is about how the Zapatista movement came about, its practice-before-theory approach, how it built autonomous institutions, and the original Good Government Boards.

Want it straight from the Zapatistas? Their own archive is Enlace Zapatista, and look especially for their 2023 explanations of the new autonomy.
